biography: Daim Hishamuddin, a name now synonymous with Singaporean motorsport, didn't grow up around roaring engines and checkered flags. His introduction to racing was almost accidental. At 16, while working part-time at a go-kart track, Daim was dared by a group of tourists to try out one of the karts. He dominated the session, leaving the tourists in the dust and sparking a passion that would reshape his life. He quickly progressed through the ranks, winning local karting championships before making the jump to single-seaters in Asia. It wasn't an easy transition; early struggles with car control and adapting to downforce nearly derailed his career. A breakthrough came during a particularly wet race at Sepang, where his raw talent and fearless approach allowed him to carve through the field, securing a podium finish against far more experienced drivers. Now at 28, Daim finds himself at the peak of his abilities, battling for championships in the Caterham 620R series, a testament to his relentless drive and unwavering belief in his own capabilities.
drivingStyle: Daim's driving style is characterized by an aggressive, late-braking approach. He thrives on pushing the car to its absolute limit, often flirting with the edge of control. His tire management, while improving, remains a work in progress; he occasionally sacrifices longevity for immediate pace. Under pressure, Daim tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to mistakes, but more often resulting in spectacular overtakes. He has a knack for finding grip where others can't, particularly in wet conditions, making him a formidable opponent in unpredictable races.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days. Tanaka always considered Daim an upstart and has made several attempts to sabotage Daim's races. The rivalry has escalated over the years, with both drivers now fiercely competitive on and off the track.

A more recent rivalry, born from a controversial collision during a championship-deciding race. Rossi accused Daim of deliberately causing the accident, while Daim maintains it was a racing incident. Their on-track battles are now some of the most hotly anticipated in the series.

Vael is known to be a more calculated driver, and he and Daim often butt heads about the best way to handle the Caterham 620R. Vael criticizes Daim's aggressive style, while Daim finds Vael too conservative.

quirks: Always wears the same faded Singapore Sling t-shirt under his race suit.
Listens to a specific playlist of 80's synth-pop on repeat before every race.
Refuses to eat anything yellow on race day, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: It's not about being the fastest; it's about being the last one to brake.
careerHighlight: Winning the Macau Grand Prix in a Formula 3 car in 2018. Despite starting from P6, Daim managed to overtake 3 drivers on the first lap and then defended his lead against a hard-charging field to secure the victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Singapore Caterham 620R Championship in 2022. The accident cost him the championship title and resulted in a broken wrist.
